questions.question: Council of ministers are collectively responsible to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __** Lok Sabha.**__

__
 
• Article 75(3)__ of the Indian Constitution makes the council of ministers collectively responsible to the house of people or the​__Lok Sabha__.
 
• 'Collective responsibility' means that the council of ministers is responsible for every action of the Government (Executive) as a single unit before the __Lok Sabha__ as they act as a bridge between the Executive and the Legislature.
 
• In case a no-confidence motion is passed against the PM, the entire Government has to resign. 

Extra facts:

 
• The First Lok Sabha was constituted on 13 April 1952 after India's first general election.
 
• **First Session of this Lok Sabha commenced on 13 May 1952.
 
• The 1st Lok Sabha lasted its full tenure of five years and was dissolved on 4 April 1957.
 
• First Lok Sabha period** - 13 April 1952- 4 April 1957
 
• **First Speaker** - Shri G.V. Mavalankar
 
• **First Deputy Speaker** - Shri M.A.Ayyangar
 
• **First Secretary-General **- Shri M. N.Kaul

questions.question: Under which pardoning power of the President, one form of punishment is substituted by a lighter form?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Article 72** of the Constitution **empowers the President to grant pardons** to persons who have been tried and convicted of any offense.
 
• Pardoning power includes:

 

 
 

 
 
**Pardon**

 
 
 
It removes both the sentence and the conviction and completely absolves the convict from all the sentences, punishments, and disqualifications.

 
 
 

 
 
**Commutation__**

 
 
 
Denotes the substitution of one form of punishment for a lighter form.

 
 
 

 
 
**Remission**

 
 
 
Reducing the period of a sentence without changing its character. For eg.10 years of strict punishment reduced to 6 years of strict punishment.

 
 
 

 
 
**Respite**

 
 
 
Delays in the imposition of the sentence but in no way modify a sentence or addresses questions of due process, guilt or innocence, due to some special fact, such as the physical disability of convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender.

 
 
 

 
 
**Reprieve**

 
 
 
A stay of the execution of a sentence (especially that of death) for a temporary period to enable the convict to have time to seek pardon or commutation from the President. Eg. A person can take a reprieve from death in the case when he wants to apply for an appeal.
